newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Korean unit may cost IPC S$45.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: Korean unit may cost IPC S$45.5 mln.

text.p: Computer company IPC Corp said on Friday it estimated its exposure to its troubled Korean unit at Singapore S$45.5 million.
IPC said in a statement to the Stock Exchange of Singapore that it had been informed its Korean subsidiary IPC Corporation (Korea) Ltd (IPCK) had defaulted in the repayment of bank's bills.
"The Company estimates that the Group's aggregate exposure to IPCK amounts to approximaely S$45.5 million, comprising of paid up share capital, account receivables and contingent liabilities.

"This exposure, if fully realised would reduce the Group's NTA (net tangible asset) backing per share by 4.55 cents, from 33.3 cents to 28.75 cents, based on the unaudited accounts of the Group as at 30 June 1996," IPC said in the statement.

A Reuters report said on Thursday that IPC's Korean unit had defaulted on repaying 570 million won worth of promissory notes to Korea First Bank. The bills were due on Wednesday, according to a bank official.
IPC said it had not been able to contact or locate the chief executive officer of IPCK and that it was investigating the matter.
Share trading in IPC has been suspended from Thursday at its request. Its stock last traded at S$0.56 prior to the suspension.
